topic: map(parseInt) returns [1, NaN, NaN]: map passes the index, which parseInt reads as the radix
text:
["1", "2", "3"].map(parseInt) returns [1, NaN, NaN]. Not [1, 2, 3].

map() calls its callback with three arguments: element, index, array. parseInt takes two: the string and the radix. So the index silently becomes the radix:

parseInt("1", 0) → 1 (radix 0 means default)
parseInt("2", 1) → NaN (radix 1 is out of range)
parseInt("3", 2) → NaN (3 isn't a binary digit)

The fix is to wrap it so only one argument gets through:

["1", "2", "3"].map((s) => parseInt(s, 10))

My rule of thumb: never pass a function with optional parameters straight into map, filter or forEach. Wrap it, or use Number when you want strict parsing (Number("12px") is NaN, parseInt("12px", 10) is 12).

Which built-in has bitten you with this "extra argument" behaviour?
